label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I ii q.94…: The ancient Germans held that robbery is not unjust…
locator: I-II q.94 a.4 co.: sicut apud Germanos olim latrocinium non reputabatur iniquum, cum tamen sit expresse contra legem naturae
interpretation: Aquinas's example (from Caesar, De bello Gallico) of natural-law knowledge failing in a proper conclusion because reason was depraved by passion, bad custom or a bad disposition of nature. Read as: the Germans held the moral judgment 'robbery is not unjust', and it is not true (robbery is expressly against the natural law). The sentence's truth-aptness is the separate claim AQUINAS-ST-I-II-Q94-A4-PRACTICAL-TRUTH.
